transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-07-14
- Time: 16:00 PDT
- Duration: ~58 minutes
- Attendees: Sofia Morales (Redwood AE), Devon Kim (Redwood SE), Jamal Ortiz (Platform Eng Manager - BlueHarbor), Priya Rao (SRE), Liam Chen (CTO), Marta Alvarez (Privacy)

Summary:
Quick console-focused demo to show request-level tracing, error analysis flows, and how to debug production regressions. Emphasis on: correlating request logs to model-level traces, KV cache inspection, fallback behavior when dedicated capacity is saturated, and security/compliance controls for enterprise deployments.

Topics covered:
- Live console walkthrough: request timeline, token-level latencies, model fallback traces
- Error analysis: identifying hallucinations vs timeouts and delta between prompt vs cache hits
- Request logs export, retention, and redaction controls (DPA concerns)
- Private deployment considerations: VPC peering, KMS integration, audit logs
- Next steps: pilot scope and log handoff for POC benchmarking

Transcript:
[00:00] Sofia Morales: Hey everyone, welcome — thanks for taking the time. I'm Sofia from Redwood, this is Devon Kim our SE. We wanted to run through the Console diagnostics and show how you can go from a noisy alert to a root cause in, um, one workflow. Jamal, thanks for organizing.

[00:12] Jamal Ortiz: Yeah, thanks. Appreciate it. We're especially interested in the request-to-model mapping, um, we've seen some 95th percentile spikes on our customer-facing routes and not sure if it's a model or infra issue.

[00:23] Devon Kim: Great, that's exactly the demo. I'll share my screen and we'll pull up a recent synthetic trace we brought — it'll look like your traffic pattern. Heads up: audio/video lag, sorry in advance if there's any stutter.

[00:36] [screen share noise] Devon Kim: Ok so top left is the request timeline overview, you can see route-level SLOs, token counts, and a latency heatmap. I'm clicking into a single slow request — on the right we get the per-stage breakdown: request ingestion, routing, model prep, KV cache lookup, generation time.

[01:05] Priya Rao: Quick question — when you say KV cache lookup, is that for prefix caching or full-response caches? We use some prefix caches in front of our app.

[01:13] Devon Kim: Good question. Redwood supports both prefix/KV caching and result caching. In the trace you can see a KV cache hit flag — when it's a hit, generation time is near-zero and most of the latency is in routing. If hit is false, you get the full model generation profile.

[01:31] Liam Chen: And how does the runtime choose kernels? We have mixed sequence lengths and sometimes the model step seems to spike CPU.

[01:37] Devon Kim: The runtime picks kernels based on model architecture and observed sequence lengths — our profiler picks a.k.a. a kernel plan. There's also a quantization profile that can change based on your Dedicated vs Hosted plan. That said, the trace will surface kernel selection and any unexpected conversions that add overhead.

[02:03] [00:02:00] Sofia Morales: To show error analysis — here's a request that returned an incoherent answer and also had a 503 from a fallback model. Notice in the timeline there's a nested span: the primary model timed out at 6s and then the fallback kicked in at 6.2s. The console shows both model traces side-by-side.

[02:28] Jamal Ortiz: That nested span view is awesome. Can you filter to all requests that invoked fallback in the last 24 hours?

[02:34] Devon Kim: Yep, filter panel on the left. I type fallback:true and it shows 42 requests. You can group by route, by user id, or by model variant. There's an export button to get raw traces as JSON for offline analysis.

[02:50] [02:50] Priya Rao: Are those exports anonymized automatically? We can't share PII with vendors.

[02:56] Sofia Morales: Good point — we have redaction rules. You can redact fields at ingest with regexes or use our built-in PII scrubbing. For private deployments, customers can enable customer-side redaction before anything hits Redwood storage. That's also in the DPA.

[03:14] Marta Alvarez: On that, do you support customer-managed keys? We need KMS and HSM integrations for keys and logs.

[03:19] Devon Kim: Yes — for Private deployments we support KMS/HSM integrations and audit log export to your side. We also ship a SOC 2+ summary; I'll include that in the follow-up.

[03:32] [03:32] Sofia Morales: Back to the trace — I'm drilling into the token-level timing. The console breaks down first token latency, steady-state token emission, and streaming handoff. You can see the model produced tokens slowly after the prefix — heavy attention cost on longer contexts shows up as a ramp in the token curve.

[03:56] Jamal Ortiz: Hmm, that ramp looks like our users who have long conversations. Are there suggestions to reduce cost and keep latency?

[04:03] Devon Kim: A few: better prefix caching for common system prompts, shorter max tokens, or dialing in a quantized model variant. We also have an Optimize tab that recommends batching windows and cache TTLs based on your traffic. For conversation-heavy routes, enabling continuous KV cache is your best win.

[04:21] [04:21] Liam Chen: About the fallback policy — can we set deterministic fallbacks (e.g., always go to small-quantized model under X latency) and also do canary rollouts?

[04:28] Devon Kim: Absolutely. Rollouts are configurable per-route: canary percentage, automatic rollback on quality deltas, and fallback tiers. The console records quality metrics tied to eval prompts so rollback can be automated.

[04:44] [04:44] Priya Rao: What about reproducing bad responses? If we have a user complaint, can we replay the exact request including prompt and model state?

[04:52] Devon Kim: Yes, the Request Playback feature replays the request against any model variant and you can toggle KV cache on/off. For privacy you can replay in a customer private deployment or in a sandbox with redacted inputs.

[05:06] [05:06] Jamal Ortiz: Can we hook that into our incident pipeline? We use PagerDuty and Slack — ideally a trace link posts to Slack with the key spans.

[05:13] Sofia Morales: We have webhooks and integrations — you can configure the alerting rules to send a trace URL, and the trace includes a short human-readable excerpt. We'll share the webhook config in the runbook.

[05:25] [05:25] Marta Alvarez: About logs retention — we need 7 years for auditability in some regulated flows. What are your retention policies and export options?

[05:32] Devon Kim: Hosted retention is tiered — default 90 days, extended paid retention options up to multi-year, plus export hooks to S3 or your logging infra. For Private, you control retention entirely on your side.

[05:45] [05:45] Sofia Morales: I'm going to demonstrate a quick error triage: here's a group of requests with high divergence score against an eval set. We can pin one anomalous request and compare token-by-token with the eval baseline; differences are highlighted.

[06:05] [06:05] Jamal Ortiz: That diff view would help us quantify regression severity for product. Is divergence a proprietary metric?

[06:11] Devon Kim: It's a composite score — perplexity delta plus semantic similarity heuristics. We show the raw components so you can tune thresholds.

[06:25] [06:25] Priya Rao: Say during a peak we hit Dedicated capacity limits — what's the graceful degradation? Do you queue requests? Failover to hosted?

[06:34] Devon Kim: Options are configurable: queue with backpressure, fallback to a cheaper model on a separate pool, or fail open with a cached response. The console shows when routing decisions are made and why (policy hit, capacity threshold).

[06:49] [06:49] Sofia Morales: I'll open a simulated incident timeline — note the routing policy change at 14:03 triggered by autoscaler lag. The trace shows requests that were re-routed to another region — you'll see increased network hop and added latency.

[07:05] [07:05] Liam Chen: That's important for us because we care about regional data residency. If fallback routes to another region, is that data movement auditable?

[07:12] Devon Kim: Yes — every route decision is audited. The trace contains metadata about model region, node id, and decision rule. For Private deployments you can restrict routes to region-only.

[07:26] [07:26] Jamal Ortiz: Can you show the search over logs for a specific user journey? We'll want to tie platform metrics back to the user session id.

[07:33] Devon Kim: Sure — filter by session_id in the left column, it surfaces every request and correlated traces, plus linked logs from your app if you ship them via our ingestion API.

[07:45] [07:45] Priya Rao: A practical thing — do you provide SDKs for structured logging so we can push context easily?

[07:50] Devon Kim: Yes we have lightweight SDKs (Python, Node) that attach trace ids and structured fields. We'll include code snippets in the runbook.

[07:59] [07:59] Sofia Morales: I'm going to intentionally trigger a model timeout — reproduce: long prompt, artificial network throttle — watch the trace.

[08:10] [08:10] [sound of keys & throttle simulation] Devon Kim: OK, you can see the span where the model timed out. Console shows the retry attempts, fallback chosen, and a summary card that recommends increasing burst capacity or enabling pre-warmed instances for that route.

[08:29] [08:29] Marta Alvarez: For the retry and fallback policy, are those logs considered part of the same request for audit purposes? We need a single correlated event.

[08:36] Devon Kim: The trace groups subspans under a parent request id, so yes — all retries and fallbacks are correlated. The export includes the parent-child relationships.

[08:47] [08:47] Jamal Ortiz: This is very promising. Two things: can we benchmark a handful of our heavy routes with your Dedicated pool and compare cost/latency vs our current infra, and second, we need formal security paperwork.

[08:58] Sofia Morales: Absolutely. Proposal: 4-week POC with dedicated pool sized to your 95th, we'll run benchmarks and provide a cost/latency report. We'll also attach the SOC 2 summary and the DPA.

[09:12] [09:12] Priya Rao: What's the timeline to spin up a small dedicated pool for POC?

[09:16] Devon Kim: We can get a small Dedicated pool provisioned in 3-5 business days once we have an initial commit and network details. For Private, provisioning timing depends on your infra but we have a documented checklist.

[09:30] [09:30] Liam Chen: One last thing — how easy is it to capture a golden prompt set for our routes to be used during rollouts and regression checks?

[09:37] Devon Kim: Console has an Evals integration: you can pin prompt sets, run batch evals on every new model or rollout, and get a quality delta. We'll guide you on seeding that with session logs.

[09:48] [09:48] Marta Alvarez: On compliance, will you sign a mutual NDAs or addenda?

[09:52] Sofia Morales: We can. Our legal ops handle NDAs, and the DPA has clauses for data handling. I'll loop in our security & legal contacts after the call.

[10:02] [10:02] Jamal Ortiz: Great — thanks, this was useful. Any closing notes?

[10:06] Sofia Morales: Recap: we'll send pilot scope + pricing, Devon will share runbook and KV cache replay video, customer to share sample logs. We'll aim to kick off POC week of 7/27. I'll follow up with links to SOC 2 and the webhook/runbook.

[10:18] [10:18] Priya Rao: Thanks. One tiny nit — sometimes model names are mis-transcribed in the console transcript exports. Are there ID references we can rely on?

[10:25] Devon Kim: Yes, every model has a stable model_id and version_id; those are included in exports to avoid ambiguity.

[10:33] [10:33] Meeting ends.
